palette.notes: The article does not cover palette; the work starts from a flat colour-coded dummy (head, neck, torso, arms, legs) so each body part is readable before any shading.

lighting: Not covered; the article is about poses and timing, not light.
silhouette: Built on a simple colour-coded dummy; legs crossing at the pass pose and arms at the extremes of their swing on contact give two clearly different silhouettes per step.

motion.timing: 8-frame cycle (article calls it the best balance of economy and fluidity), also shown at 4 and 6 frames. Reference: a 72-frame 60 fps slice reduced to 8 keys. No per-frame ms given.
principles: key poses: contact, down, pass, swing

texture: Clothing folds kept minimal, with consistent anchor points and fold direction across all frames so they do not flicker.
camera: Side view, character walking in place; no camera.

acting.enters: No staging shown; the cycle is a loop in place.
acting.acts: Personality comes from the gait: a tight arm swing reads stiff and businesslike, a fuller swing past the hips reads peppy and elegant.
acting.depth: Single sprite at one scale; the article warns that labour grows quickly with sprite size, so plan size, detail and frame count together.

techniques: 8-frame walk: contact, down, pass, swing, then the mirror of those four
lowest point on contact, tallest on the pass
head height follows a triangle wave, not a sine wave
arm swing width sets the character: tight = stiff, wide = peppy
trim live-action reference to one loop, then reduce to key frames
one-pixel secondary shifts on contact sell weight
start from a colour-coded body-part dummy before detail
feel: 8 keys + triangle-wave bob + arm swing width as personality = a walk that says who the character is
for_fred: Give Fred's swim a 4-key cycle (contact-like push, glide, pass, reach) with a triangle-wave bob, not a smooth sine float. Use cycle shape as character: Pixie gets a wide, peppy stride, Fred a tight, fussy one, so a single walk across the frame already tells who they are.
